props.name: status
props.default: home; away draws its badge only from s44 up

props.name: isYou
props.default: false

props.name: isAdmin
props.default: false; the key badge is drawn only from s44 up

components.semantics: One image node named by semanticLabel (required, not empty), which holds the whole description (name, you, admin, away); the initials, the badges and the outline are excluded. A node of its own under a parent that does not merge; under a parent that merges its children (a MergeSemantics row) its label joins the row's. Status and role are drawn as shapes: moon badge (away), dashed outline without fill (invited), key badge (admin), inset dark ring (you). The away and admin badges are drawn only from s44 up: on s28 and s36 they are left out, so say them in semanticLabel and in the text next to the pebble. The away badge hangs at the bottom trailing corner and the admin key at the top trailing corner (the board puts the key at the bottom too, where it would cover the status badge). The pebble is always a square: exactly its side at text scale 1, growing continuously with larger text. Two initials up to MW fit at every size; wider pairs (WW) grow s28 and s36 by a pixel or two. From s44 up the side reserves room for the badge squares in every state, so pebbles of a size stay equal. On s44+ a badge may cover the tip of an accent or a descender on two-letter initials; capitals are never covered

Decorative and excluded from semantics: the dot has no label. It always sits next to the text that names the status and is never the only cue (home and busy differ only by hue), so it must never stand alone

props.name: count
props.default: AppBadge.count: the number, 99+ beyond 99

props.name: label
props.default: AppBadge.label: a short text

props.name: tone
props.default: primary for count, soft for label

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: replaces the visible text for assistive technology

components.semantics: The visible number or label is read as it is. With semanticLabel the badge is one labeled node ("3 unread") and its text is excluded. Like any semantic child it merges into a parent that merges its children (a MergeSemantics row reads the row label and the badge label as one); under a parent that does not merge it is a node of its own. Text reaches 4.5:1 on every fill; the fill carries no meaning. Callers hide the badge at 0

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: null leaves the ring out of semantics

props.name: value
props.default: null: in use with no known end, a breathing arc; 0 to 1 otherwise, clamped; must be finite

props.name: tone
props.default: primary

props.name: size
props.default: AppSizes.ring (56); grows with a large label

props.name: label
props.default: text in the middle

props.name: semanticValue
props.default: required with a value, for example 11 of 15 done

components.semantics: With a semanticLabel the ring is one node: the label names what it measures and, with a value, semanticValue says how far it is (an in-use ring never has a value); the drawing and the middle label are excluded. Null excludes the ring. Like any semantic child it merges into a parent that merges its children. The arc breathes only when animations are enabled, and stands still at full opacity otherwise. A value that is not finite is drawn as 0

props.name: ageDays
props.default: calendar days since the task was last done, counted by the app in the home's time zone; zero or less is fresh

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: null leaves the bar out of semantics: the age text beside it says it

components.semantics: Image named by semanticLabel with container: true when the label is non-empty (a node of its own under a parent that does not merge; it merges into a merging parent like any semantic child), else decorative and excluded because the age text beside it carries the meaning. It always sits beside that text in a fixed-width column and is never the only cue: the track is the sunken surface, so the end of the bar is not visible. The fill is 100, 85, 60 or 25 percent and no danger color is used

props.name: member
props.default: name, initials, joinOrder, status, isYou, isAdmin and the spoken description (semanticLabel)

props.name: subtitle
props.default: second line under the name

props.name: trailing
props.default: text at the end of the row; a status dot sits before it (none while invited)

components.semantics: One merged node, not interactive: member.semanticLabel (it names the member and says you, admin and away), then the subtitle, then the trailing text. The visible name, the pebble and the dot add nothing of their own, so nothing is said twice
notes: Layout: the pebble and the texts take up to two thirds of the row and the trailing text one third, beside each other. When the longest word of the name or the subtitle does not fit beside the pebble in its share, or the longest word of the trailing text does not fit in its third, the trailing text and its dot move under the texts and the texts take the width the pebble leaves (as the home AppTopBar does with its buttons), so no word breaks at large text. At a text scale of 1.0 in a phone column the row is laid out as before.
A small private render object lays the row out, with intrinsic and dry layout, not a LayoutBuilder, so the golden harness can measure it.
One case is left: a word wider than the whole row. It wraps by its letters, so all of it stays visible at 200% (WCAG 1.4.4); the name is never cut with an ellipsis.

The row keeps the baseline of the name, so it lines up with a neighbor in a baseline-aligned Row. The status dot sits on the middle of the first line of the trailing text. The row-long state has a long name, subtitle and trailing text, so the large text scenarios of its golden show the stacked layout.

props.name: item
props.default: id, name and the appliance glyph

props.name: inUse

props.name: statusLabel

props.default: replaces the visible texts for assistive technology

components.semantics: One focusable button named by semanticLabel ("Washer, in use by Carlos, 34 minutes"), activated by tap, Enter and Space; the ring, the glyph and the visible texts add nothing of their own. Drawn at least 44 tall, hit area at least 48

props.name: caption

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: spoken description of the whole tile

props.name: occupants
props.default: empty; drawn as s36 pebbles at the end of the footer line, wrapped under the beacons and start-aligned when they do not fit on one line

props.name: beacons
props.default: empty; pinned at the bottom start, wrapping onto more lines, each its own button

components.semantics: One container node named by semanticLabel ("Bathroom, occupied by Carlos, 12 minutes"), not interactive; the name, caption, lock and pebbles add nothing of their own. Each beacon stays its own focusable button, a child of that node. The state is also said by the caption, never by color or outline alone
notes: Not interactive: no onTap yet. The FloorplanMap organism needs one, and a tappable tile around its beacon buttons needs its own semantics design.
The contract states archived and draw are not drawn: the board shows neither, and the floorplan hides archived rooms. The RoomDrawBoard organism draws the tile in its draw form.

props.default: id, title and ageDays (calendar days since it was last done, counted by the app in the home time zone)

props.name: subtitle
props.default: line under the title that says who did it last, when and where

props.name: logAgainSemanticLabel

components.semantics: The title and the subtitle are one merged text node; the freshness bar is excluded because the subtitle says the age. The log control is its own focusable button named by logAgainSemanticLabel ("Log Clean the kitchen again"), activated by tap, Enter and Space. The row itself is not tappable. Calm: no danger color, never who is behind

components.semantics: One container node named by semanticLabel ("Absence, Luis, until Fri 6 Nov"), not interactive; the glyph and the visible title add nothing of their own, and the compact form says the same with no title. The kind is told by its glyph and title, never by color alone, and a flat edge is only a shape, so the label says that the event goes on

props.name: subtitle

props.name: activityLabel

props.name: onActivity

props.name: me

props.name: accountLabel

props.name: backLabel
props.default: pushed only; spoken name of the back button

props.name: onBack
props.default: pushed only

props.name: actionLabel
props.default: pushed only; null or empty leaves the action out

props.name: onAction
props.default: pushed only; null disables the action

components.semantics: The bar is its own semantics group, so under a Card or a list item the title stays a heading node of its own and the buttons stay buttons. The parts are read in order: the title, the subtitle, the bell, the account (the title, the back button, the action on the pushed bar). The subtitle is plain text. The bell, the account pebble, the back arrow and the action are focusable buttons named by their label props, which are never empty (the badge on the bell is merged into its button and read once, as part of activityLabel); targets are 44 drawn with a 48 hit area. The bar pads itself by the top inset of the screen (no SafeArea needed). It mirrors in right-to-left text, back arrow included, and grows with large text instead of clipping: above a text scale of 1.3 the bell and the account of the home bar drop under the title, and the badge sits beside the bell glyph, never over it
components.key: topBar.<part> (title, subtitle, activity, account, back, action)

props.name: destinations
props.default: one to four: id, icon, label, badgeCount (0 draws none) and semanticLabel of each destination

props.name: onSelected
props.default: called with the tapped index, also when it is the selected one

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: name of the navigation landmark

components.semantics: A navigation landmark named by semanticLabel. Each destination is one focusable button in a mutually exclusive group, with a selected state, named by its semanticLabel (which must contain the visible label) or else its label; a badge count is merged into that name and read once. Destinations are 52 tall and at least 48 wide. The selected one has a primary-soft plate with a 2 px primary border and ink text, so selection is not color alone. At most 4 destinations with short single-word labels, on a screen at least 360 wide (the smallest target; at 320 a word like Calendario breaks at 1.3). The one documented text scale cap of the system: labels and badge counts stop growing at 1.3, like Material NavigationBar (_kMaxLabelTextScaleFactor); the semantics keep the full label. The surface runs under the bottom inset. The order mirrors in right-to-left text

props.name: closeLabel
props.default: spoken name of the close button

components.semantics: The header is its own semantics group: under a Card or a list item the title stays a heading node of its own, read before the close button, and the button stays a button. The close button is a focusable button named by closeLabel, which is never empty, 44 drawn with a 48 hit area. The drag handle is decorative and excluded from semantics. A long title wraps and the header grows while the close button stays at the top end; the layout mirrors in right-to-left text. The title is centered on the 48 hit area of the close button (15 below the handle, board 12)

props.name: actionLabel
props.default: null or empty leaves the action out

props.name: onAction
props.default: null disables the action

components.semantics: One group: the title and the body are a single text node read together, followed by the action as a focusable button named by its label (44 drawn, 48 hit area). The dashed plan motif is decorative and excluded. The copy never blames anyone. Content is centered and wraps with large text instead of clipping, so at large text it can be taller than the screen: it must sit in a scrollable screen

props.name: tone
props.default: info

props.name: actionLabel
props.default: null or empty leaves the action out

props.name: onAction
props.default: null disables the action

props.name: visible
props.default: true; changing it plays the enter or the exit over motion.snackbar, at once under disableAnimations

components.semantics: A live region named by message (never empty), announced once when it appears; the glyph and the text are excluded. The action is a focusable button named by actionLabel after the message (44 drawn, 48 hit area, light focus ring, an overlay of the soft primary, a dimmer disabled state); an action wider than a quarter of the bar moves under the message, end-aligned, as Material does, so the message keeps its words whole at 2.0. The tone is a glyph (check or circled exclamation mark), never color alone and never a danger color. No timer: the app decides when to show and dismiss it by flipping visible. After the exit the bar takes no space and leaves the semantics and the focus order, and while it leaves the action cannot take focus

props.name: entry
props.default: id, glyph (icon), tone (neutral or busy), text (a list of runs, each with a strong flag, in the word order of the language) and meta (muted line under it)

props.name: unread
props.default: unread: a dot at the end of the row

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: spoken description of the entry: it says whether the entry is unread ("Unread. Carlos finished your washer") and holds the visible text in the same words (WCAG 2.5.3)

components.semantics: One focusable button named by semanticLabel, activated by tap, Enter and Space. The tile, the texts and the unread dot add nothing of their own, so nothing is said twice. Unread is a shape (the dot) and is in the spoken label, never color alone. Calm: busy is amber, never a danger color, never who is behind
notes: Board gaps: the tile glyph is 18 (size.glyph-lg) where the board draws 20, and the tile corner is radius.sm (10) where the board draws 12.

Board gaps: the row is 64 tall with 12 of padding where the board draws 68 with 14, and the 2 px between the message and the meta line is not drawn. None of 14, 2 or 68 is a token, and a row that is 64 like the member row keeps the list rhythm.
The line is a list of runs (ActivityText with a strong flag) so the bold part can sit anywhere, as in 'Room draw: you got Bedroom 1'.

props.name: value
props.default: home or away: the selected side

props.name: onChanged
props.default: called with the other side only; choosing the selected side does nothing

props.name: homeLabel
props.default: label of the home side

props.name: awayLabel
props.default: label of the away side

props.name: semanticLabel
props.default: name of the group for assistive technology ("Your presence")

components.semantics: A radio group named by semanticLabel with two toggle buttons (homeLabel, awayLabel), exactly one checked and in a mutually exclusive group, each focusable and activated by tap, Enter and Space. The glyphs and the second drawing of each face (see notes) add nothing. The selected side is the only one under a filled thumb (3:1 against the track) and both sides have their own glyph and label, so the state is never color alone
notes: Board gaps: the board builds the sides from two AppButtons with a fill each, but the away side is filled with presence-away and AppButton has no variant for it, so the sides are Material TextButtons under one filled thumb that slides.

Board gaps: the track gets a 1 px outline border the board does not draw, so it keeps 3:1 against the page and a card. With it the sides are 54 tall where the board draws 56 (64 minus 4 and 4), and their corner is 11 where the board draws 12.

While the thumb slides every label and glyph is drawn twice, in the muted ink clipped to what is outside the thumb and in the on-color clipped to the thumb, so no color is blended and every pixel reads on every frame. At rest each face is drawn once. The second drawing is excluded from semantics, pointer and focus. The thumb jumps when animations are off. Each face sets its own text style, so a line limit, an italic or an underline around the switch does not change a label while the thumb slides.
The contract names a Presence type: it is a new two-value enum (home, away) because MemberStatus also has invited.

props.name: label
props.default: visible label of the ready button ("Who's home?"), which names it

props.name: onKnock
props.default: called by a tap while the button is ready

props.name: cooldown
props.default: null: ready. Set: inert, with the share of the wait left (remaining, 0 to 1, never NaN), a label ("Asked"), the time left ("11 min") and the spoken sentence (semanticLabel)

components.semantics: One node in both states, never replaced: a button, focusable, with a focus action and a focused flag. Ready: enabled, named by label, a tap calls onKnock. Cooldown: the same node marked disabled, without the tap action, named by cooldown.semanticLabel ("Asked who's home. You can ask again in 11 minutes"). The visible texts, the ring and Material's own node add nothing. The Material button is the same widget in both states and stays focusable and inert in the wait, so keyboard focus stays on it when the wait starts and the next Tab goes to the next control. The wait is told by words and a ring, never color alone. Calm: no danger color, no blame
notes: The contract lists availableAt: DateTime? and now: DateTime. The design system keeps no clock and no dates, so the app counts the wait and passes KnockCooldown (remaining share, label, time left, spoken sentence) instead.
Board gaps: the glyph is 18 (size.glyph-lg) where the board draws 20, and the 2 px between the ring and the two lines of text, and between them, is not drawn (there is no 2 px token).
Board gaps: the ring is AppProgressRing at 24 with its 4 px stroke where the board draws a 2.5 px one, and its track has the same color as the sunken fill, so only the arc shows.

The semantics node is the same one before and after the wait starts (a test compares its id and checks it is still focused), so a screen reader keeps its cursor. How a given screen reader announces the change of name and enabled state is not verified on a device.

props.name: code
props.default: the code as shown, already grouped by the app ("4829 1736"); it wraps at the spaces and always reads left to right

props.name: label
props.default: caption over the code, which also names it for assistive technology ("Your personal code")

props.name: copyLabel
props.default: label of the copy button

props.name: copiedLabel
props.default: label of the copy button once copied

props.name: shareLabel
props.default: label of the share button

props.name: copied
props.default: false; true shows copiedLabel and a check on the copy button. The app must announce the copy too, for example with an AppSnackbar

props.name: onCopy
props.default: the app does the clipboard

props.name: onShare
props.default: the app does the share sheet

components.semantics: The code is one node named by label whose value is the code spelled out character by character; the visible texts add nothing. Copy and share are their own focusable buttons named by their visible labels, activated by tap, Enter and Space. The card is not interactive. Copied is a label and a check, never color alone
notes: The contract lists code, onCopy and onShare. Every visible string is a prop, so label, copyLabel, copiedLabel and shareLabel are added, with copied for the state the app sets.

Board gaps: the board's buttons have no glyphs and these show the copy, check and share ones; the buttons are AppButton secondary, 52 tall with a radius of 16, where the board draws 48 and 12; the card radius is radius.sm (10) where the board draws 12.
The buttons stack at large text, which the board's two-column grid cannot. The dashed edge is decoration in the hairline color, as on RoomTile, because the card is not a control.
A code that is not grouped (eight digits with no space) is one word: at 2.0x it can be wider than the card and is cut inside the word. The app groups it.
